sections.overview: This Guianan cichlid was described from Suriname and is known from the Suriname River drainage. ITIS accepts the name established by Kullander and Nijssen in 1989.
sections.identification: Six flank bars, the last extending onto the caudal peduncle, help distinguish it from G. abalios.
sections.habitat: It occurs in clear, lightly stained or black waters along gently sloping sandy margins.
sections.diet: Like other Geophagus, it sifts substrate; the broader genus diet includes invertebrates, plant matter, seeds and detritus.
sections.behavior: It is gregarious outside breeding, with juveniles especially prone to form groups.
sections.reproduction: Its breeding mode is unconfirmed and should not be inferred from other members of the surinamensis group.
sections.ecology: Unlike Xingu-basin G. argyrostictus, this species is in the G. surinamensis group. The lot also includes Panamanian G. crassilabris.
sections.conservation: FishBase lists Least Concern, assessed on 27 December 2020; this global category does not establish that every local population is secure.
